generated_content.title: Fox Develops Two-Hour Remake of Cult Classic 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show'
generated_content.overview: Fox is producing a two-hour remake of the 1975 cult classic 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show,' directed, executive-produced, and choreographed by Kenneth Ortega. The special, tentatively titled 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show Event,' is casting-contingent and will be filmed in advance. The project is timed to celebrate the 40th anniversary of the film, which has grossed over $112 million.
key_points: The remake is the latest musical to get the small-screen treatment.
Kenneth Ortega is attached to direct, executive-produce, and choreograph the special.
The special will be produced by Fox 21 Television Studios and The Jackal Group.
This isn't the first attempt at adapting 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show,' with a previous Fox adaptation planned for the 30th anniversary in 2002.
important_facts: $112 million grossed by the original film, which still plays in theaters across the country.
Kenneth Ortega's credits include 'Gilmore Girls,' 'This Is It,' and 'Hocus Pocus.'
Fox has a live musical production of 'Grease' scheduled to air on January 31, 2016.
NBC recently announced plans to air a live version of 'The Wiz' later this year.
implications: The remake may attract a new audience to the cult classic.
The special's production and airing may impact Fox's programming strategy.
The 40th anniversary celebration may boost the original film's popularity.
generated_content.conclusion: The Fox-developed remake of 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show' is a significant development in the cult classic's continued popularity, with potential implications for Fox's programming and the original film's enduring fan base.
